- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75+), then sharply correct downward — model fails to capture this “rebound” or “mean reversion” effect.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends (e.g., 68–71 range) — fails to recognize support levels or mean reversion.
- Forecast bias is often toward higher prices, especially when historical mean is above 70 — model systematically overpredicts.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often takes 2–3 days to adjust downward.
- When price spikes occur, model overreacts with exaggerated upward forecasts, then fails to correct — creates “overshoot + lag” pattern.
- Model underestimates volatility in the 68–72 range — fails to account for short-term noise or “whipsaw” behavior.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values when historical 30-day average is above 71 — model doesn’t adjust for recent mean reversion.
- Model tends to underestimate true price when it’s near recent low (e.g., 68–70) — fails to recognize “bottoming” or “support” behavior.
- Model overestimates price when recent 30-day average is above 73 — fails to recognize “overbought” or “peak” behavior.
